                                                                                                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      The member function push_back in the scope of ara::core::Vector inserts a passed element at the end of the container by copying [SWS_CORE_01363]. It is defined via header #include "ara/core/vector.h", takes a reference to a constant value const T &x, and has no return value (void) [SWS_CORE_01363]. The call occurs synchronously in the caller's context.
                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      The specification deviates from [vector] in that the function is declared as conditionally noexcept: It is guaranteed to be non-throwing if and only if std::is_nothrow_copy_assignable<T>::value applies [SWS_CORE_01363]. Accordingly, exception safety is defined as “conditionally exception safe” [SWS_CORE_01363]. Specific error codes as well as error messages via DET or DEM are not defined for this function.
                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                      Interaction and related requirements
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      For movable objects, ara::core::Vector provides overload void push_back(T &&x), whose noexcept property is analogously coupled to std::is_nothrow_move_assignable<T>::value [SWS_CORE_01364]. In contrast, push_back in ara::core::BasicString has no noexcept guarantee and is classified as “not exception safe” [SWS_CORE_03083].
                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                      Interpretation: The internal memory and reallocation behavior upon insertion, apart from the specific noexcept declaration, is likely to follow the requirements of the C++ standard for [vector].
                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                      This usage note is based on the specification of AUTOSAR Adaptive in release R25-11.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          function push_back [SWS_CORE_01364]
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          void push_back (T &&x) noexcept(std::is_nothrow_move_assignable< T >::value);
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          As per corresponding usage in [vector] except for the following deviations: 1. Function is conditionally noexcept: (see [vector.modifiers])

  Provenance
  Open questions (2)
  

                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          The member function push_back of ara::core::Vector serves to synchronously append an element to the end of the vector using move semantics ([SWS_CORE_01364]). It is provided via header #include "ara/core/vector.h", takes an rvalue reference T &&x, and has no return value (void) ([SWS_CORE_01364]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding error handling and exception behavior, the following properties apply:
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                            

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The method is classified as conditionally exception safe (conditionally exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_01364]).
                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The noexcept guarantee is tied to the type: noexcept(std::is_nothrow_move_assignable<T>::value) ([SWS_CORE_01364]). If the move assignment operator of T is not declared as exception-free, exceptions are likely to occur during memory allocations or element moves.
                                                                                                                                                                                                            • 

                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          The functionality follows the usual semantics in [vector], but deviates due to the conditional noexcept declaration ([SWS_CORE_01364]). Since the operation mutates the container, concurrent accesses to the same instance are likely not thread-safe without external synchronization.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          In interaction among the interfaces, this move variant complements the copy overload push_back(const T &x) ([SWS_CORE_01363]), which is analogously coupled to is_nothrow_copy_assignable. To be distinguished from this is the identically named member function in ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03083]), which appends single characters and is defined as not exception safe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                          This usage note was generated automatically and is based on the requirements of the specification.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              function reserve [SWS_CORE_01347]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              void reserve (size_type n);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              As per corresponding usage in [vector] except for the following deviations: 1. if (n < max_size()) IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std:: length_error

  AI-GENERATED

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The member function reserve of class ara::core::Vector serves for memory reservation for vector instances according to [SWS_CORE_01347]. It is called synchronously and provided via header file ara/core/vector.h. The function takes parameter n of type size_type and has no return value. The basic behavior corresponds to the usual semantics of std::vector::reserve from the ISO C++ standard.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Error Handling and Violations
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Deviating from the ISO C++ standard, no exception of type std::length_error is thrown in the event of an error, but rather a IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is triggered [SWS_CORE_01347]. For this, the specification cites condition n < max_size(), where an exceeding of the maximum capacity is presumably meant. In addition, according to the specification, the operation is explicitly declared as not exception safe (not exception safe) [SWS_CORE_01347].
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              


                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Interaction and Boundary Conditions
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Triggering IsoStdLengthErrorViolation conforms to the uniform error concept in ara::core and is found analogously in ara::core::BasicString::reserve according to [SWS_CORE_03054]. Since a call to reserve can trigger internal reallocations, the function is not thread-safe under concurrent access to the same instance and requires external synchronization.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  function resize [SWS_CORE_01350]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  void resize (size_type sz);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  As per corresponding usage in [vector] except for the following deviations: 1. if (sz > max_size()) IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std:: length_error

  AI-GENERATED
  unreviewed
  Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: e1f4cdbd6da3
  Provenance
  Open questions (1)
  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The member function resize adapts the number of elements contained in the container synchronously to the desired target size sz ([SWS_CORE_01350]). It belongs to class ara::core::Vector and is included via the header file #include "ara/core/vector.h" ([SWS_CORE_01350]). The functional behavior is based on the ISO C++ specification of std::vector: if the container shrinks, excess elements are erased; if it grows, additional elements are created via value-initialization.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  In case of an error, the function intentionally deviates from the behavior of the standard library: if the requested size sz is greater than max_size(), a IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is thrown instead of std::length_error ([SWS_CORE_01350]). The specification marks the function as not exception-safe (not exception safe) ([SWS_CORE_01350]). Callers must therefore ensure that capacity limits are respected in order to avoid a violation at runtime.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Regarding concurrency, the method is not reentrant for the same instance: modifying concurrent calls on the same object are likely to lead to data corruption without external synchronization (interpretation: analogous thread-safety rules as for ISO C++ containers). If newly appended elements are not to be default-initialized, but rather filled with a copy of a specified value, the overloaded variant with parameter const T& must be selected ([SWS_CORE_01351]). Class ara::core::BasicString provides a correspondingly analogous interface pair with identical error handling on limit violations ([SWS_CORE_03058], [SWS_CORE_03059]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      function resize [SWS_CORE_01351]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      void resize (size_type sz, const T &c);
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      As per corresponding usage in [vector] except for the following deviations: 1. if (sz > max_size()) IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is raised instead of std:: length_error

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      use
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The member function resize of class ara::core::Vector ([SWS_CORE_01351]) from the header file #include "ara/core/vector.h" changes the number of elements in the container to the specified target size sz. In the event of an enlargement, the function initializes newly added elements with copies of the passed value c ([SWS_CORE_01351]). The call is processed synchronously and has no return value (void).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Error Handling and Exception Safety
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The behavior largely corresponds to the standard container std::vector, but deviates deliberately in case of an error: if the parameter sz exceeds the maximum value max_size(), a IsoStdLengthErrorViolation is thrown instead of the standard exception std::length_error ([SWS_CORE_01351]). The specification explicitly marks the function as not exception safe ([SWS_CORE_01351]). If errors occur during allocation or when copying c, no guarantees exist for restoring the original object state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Restrictions and Interaction
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Due to the lack of exception safety, a failure is likely to result in an inconsistent container, which is why callers should check in advance whether sufficient capacity is available. If new elements are to be default-constructed instead, the overload resize(size_type sz) without an initialization value is provided ([SWS_CORE_01350]). Identical error behavior with the throwing of IsoStdLengthErrorViolation and classification as not exception-safe is found analogously in ara::core::BasicString ([SWS_CORE_03058], [SWS_CORE_03059]).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          function shrink_to_fit [SWS_CORE_01349]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The member function shrink_to_fit() of class ara::core::Vector serves according to [SWS_CORE_01349] to reduce the memory capacity to the amount required for the current elements in accordance with requirement [vector]. The function is declared via header file #include "ara/core/vector.h", takes no parameters, and yields no return value (void) [SWS_CORE_01349]. The call is made synchronously on the instance.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Regarding error behavior, no error codes or error messages (DET/DEM) are defined. The function is explicitly classified in the specification as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_01349]. Interpretation: If the internal reallocation of memory fails, there is presumably no guarantee regarding the preservation of the previous container state.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The restrictions of sequential data structures apply to concurrency and call context: Concurrent calls on the same instance are likely not reentrant and not thread-safe without external synchronization. No parallel read or write accesses to the vector may take place during execution.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          A directly related behavior is defined for strings in [SWS_CORE_03056]: Class ara::core::BasicString also provides a function shrink_to_fit() via #include "ara/core/string.h" that is based on [basic.string] and likewise classified as not exception safe [SWS_CORE_03056].
